newsitem.title: GERMANY: Trichet says ECB independence guaranteed.
newsitem.headline: Trichet says ECB independence guaranteed.

text.p: Jean-Claude Trichet, head of the Bank of France, said on Monday that the European Central Bank's independence was guaranteed by the Maastricht treaty and that this would ensure price stability.
Trichet, attending a regional central bank meeting in the German town of Mainz, said European monetary union was a credible process which would create an environment of stability.
"The euro must, and will, have the legacy of the most solid currencies in Europe," he said.
Throwing his support behind European monetary union, Trichet said, "European monetary union is a credible process, It will create an environment of stability."
The single currency would also foster reform and promote econoic growth, he added.
But he warned that adequate economic convergence was necessary.
"Convergence is essential after EMU as well as before," he said.
Europe plans to launch a single currency in 1999 grouping those currencies which meet economic criteria laid down in the Maastricht treaty.
